name: windows-physx-slim-build
title: Workflow that builds a slim Windows PhysX archive from the existing bin.zip (no rebuild)
issue: Approved by the user 2026-10-13 ("yeah sounds good, make sure it links"). Background (measured from the zip index): the release asset https://github.com/EpicNicks/N2Engine/releases/download/physx-dependencies/bin.zip is 1.34 GB compressed, 3.7 GB unpacked (358 files): GPU files 1766 MB unpacked (PhysXGpu_64.dll 345 MB release / 511 MB debug, plus *Gpu_static_64.lib the engine never links), 144 PhysX snippet exes and their PDBs 1518 MB, .map/.exp, checked and profile folders. The engine's CMake (root CMakeLists.txt ~l.34-75) uses only: debug and release PhysX_64, PhysXCommon_64, PhysXFoundation_64, PhysXCooking_64 (shared, dll + import lib), PhysXExtensions_static_64 and PhysXPvdSDK_static_64 (static libs), and optionally PhysXGpu_64 (dll + import lib; the existing check is for the debug PhysXGpu_64.dll). Scope (PR 1, a new workflow only): add .github/workflows/physx-windows-slim.yml with triggers workflow_dispatch (inputs: source_url default the bin.zip URL above, release_tag default `physx-dependencies-windows-5.6.1`, publish boolean default false), push of tags `physx-windows-*`, and pull_request limited to `paths: ['.github/workflows/physx-windows-slim.yml']` for dry runs (PR runs never publish). Run on windows-latest or ubuntu-latest (your choice, justify). Steps: download the source zip (record its sha256 and size in the job summary; if you can, fail when it differs from the sha256 the job computes the first time, by printing it so the orchestrator can pin it later); build the keep-list from the ACTUAL root CMakeLists.txt (parse the library and DLL names it lists, do not hard-code a guess: print the list), extract only: for config in debug and release: the dlls and libs named above (including every import lib the dlls need), PhysXGpu_64.dll + PhysXGpu_64.lib (+ their .pdb) and the .pdb of each kept dll/lib that exists; drop snippet exes/pdbs, all other exes, .map/.exp, the checked/profile folders, and every *Gpu_static*.lib (not linked). Keep the original layout `bin/win.x86_64.vc143.mt/{debug,release}/...` so it extracts at external/PhysX/physx exactly like bin.zip. Produce `physx-windows-x86_64-5.6.1-slim.zip` deterministically (sorted entries, fixed mtimes, fixed compression level) plus a `.sha256` file and a MANIFEST.txt inside the zip listing every file with its size and the sha256 of the source zip (provenance: the original build recipe is unknown to the user, so say so). VERIFY MORE THAN FILE PRESENCE: a verification job on windows-latest that extracts the slim zip over a clean checkout's external/PhysX/physx and configures + builds the engine with PhysX ON in Debug and in Release (or at least runs the same cmake configure and builds the physics test target and runs the PhysX-dependent tests, as the existing windows legs do) using the slim files instead of bin.zip, to prove it links and loads (the PhysX DLLs must be found next to the test executables and the physics tests must pass); keep it as lean as the legs allow (reuse tests.yml steps, e.g. Vulkan SDK install only if needed) and say what was verified. Upload the zip and checksum as workflow artifacts always; only when publish=true or on a tag push upload them to the release `physx-dependencies-windows-5.6.1` on EpicNicks/N2Engine (create it if missing, no --clobber, contents: write only on the publish job). Do not publish and do not create tags yourself; the orchestrator publishes after merge. Also report: the compressed and unpacked sizes of the slim zip versus bin.zip (expected about 500 MB compressed / 1 GB unpacked) and the exact file list in the ledger notes. If the verification build cannot be made to pass without a design decision, report needsUser.
acceptance: The PR dry run produces the slim zip and its manifest, and the verification job configures, builds and runs the PhysX-dependent tests in Debug and Release against it
Sizes before and after and the file list are recorded in the ledger notes
Existing Tests jobs unaffected and green
notes: Reviewer: publishing only on explicit dispatch/tag (never pull_request), minimal permissions, pinned action versions like tests.yml, no secrets, no --clobber, the keep-list derived from CMake not guessed, GPU dll and import lib kept in both configs, the verification really uses the slim files (not a cached bin.zip: check cache keys and that bin.zip is not downloaded in that job). Unverified: the enable step (PR 2) that makes the Windows legs consume the asset.
